capitals.name: Karasahr (Yanqi)
capitals.note: 'In 856, this group of Uyghurs received royal recognition from the Tang dynasty ... At this time, their capital was in Karasahr (Yanqi)'; 843 is the occupation year, the capital's earlier years are not stated.

capitals.name: Qocho (Gaochang, winter capital)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Winter capital: Qocho (Gaochang/Qara-Khoja, near Turpan)'; Xizhou (Gaochang) was taken in 866; Zhang Chengfeng of the Guiyi Circuit held it 904-911. Kept to 1370: the page names no later seat (last known ruler governor Ching Timur, 1352).

capitals.name: Beshbalik (summer capital)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Summer capital: Beshbalik (Jimsar County, also called Tingzhou)'. Taken in 866. Kept to 1370: the page names no later seat (last known ruler governor Ching Timur, 1352).

correction.text: Karasahr (Yanqi) and Kucha, 'taking them from the Tibetan Empire'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 843-865: Cliopatria's first Qocho shape begins in 860 and already holds Turfan and Beshbalik, which the page says were taken in 866. 'In 843 ... occupied Karasahr and Kucha'; 856 Tang recognition, capital at Karasahr. The page gives no area.

correction.text: From 866: Cliopatria's 860 shape without its 213 Gansu cells (92.9-96.9 E, 39.5-42.1 N), the Guiyi Circuit's Shazhou and Guazhou side: 'In 880, Qocho attacked Shazhou (Dunhuang) but was repelled'. The 860-865 years are covered by the 843-865 keyframe (Karashahr and Kucha only), because the page puts Gaochang, Beshbalik and Changbaliq in 866

keyframe_review.note: 860-887, 0.58 M km2 (2,324 cells; no area on the page): Karashahr and Kucha (Kuqa 100 of 106 cells within 100 km), Turfan, Beshbalik and Changbaliq in the north (Dzungaria 491 cells), and 213 Gansu cells. The shape holds from 866 ('In 866 ... captured Xizhou (Gaochang), Tingzhou (Beshbalik), Changbaliq ... and Luntai from the Guiyi Circuit'); the Gansu cells are the Guiyi Circuit's (880: Qocho 'attacked Shazhou (Dunhuang) but was repelled'). Hami (Yizhou) is almost outside it (24 of 114 cells within 100 km) and is added in 876.

The kingdom 'became a vassal of the Qara Khitai' in 1128 (body text; the infobox says 1132), after which Cliopatria's Kara-Khitans shape contains this land (2,309 of 2,320 cells); 1128-1138 is the vassal period of a living Qocho, not its end, so the shape holds for the whole 1126-1138 span.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1139-1369: Cliopatria's Qocho row ends in 1138 and its Kara-Khitans shape (1139-1219) then Mongol and Chagatai shapes contain the land. The kingdom kept its idiqut: 'In 1209, the Kara-Khoja ruler Baurchuk Art Tekin declared his allegiance to the Mongols under Genghis Khan'; infobox 'Vassal state of the Mongol Empire (1209-1335)'; 'Qocho continued exist as a vassal to the Mongols of the Yuan dynasty, and were allied to the Yuan against the Chagatai Khanate'; 1308 the Yuan emperor granted Nolen Tekin the title Prince of Gaochang; 'In 1352, Ching Timur iduq-qut ... was the last known ruler governor of the kingdom'; 'By the 1370s, the Kingdom of Qocho ceased to exist.' The extent is unverified (page silent, the Tarim Basin page lists only 'Uyghur rule (9th-13th century)' for Turfan); the Chagatai conquest of Hami is undated on the page. Confidence 1 for the shape.

region.text: Karasahr (Yanqi) and Kucha, 'taking them from the Tibetan Empire'

ledger.note: 843: the Uyghurs under Pangtele take Karasahr and Kucha from Tibet. 'In 843, a group of Uyghurs migrated southward under the leadership of Pangtele, and occupied Karasahr and Kucha, taking them from the Tibetan Empire'; infobox 'Established 843'; 856: Tang recognition.

region.text: Xizhou (Gaochang), Tingzhou (Beshbalik), Changbaliq (near Ürümqi) and Luntai

ledger.note: 866: Pugu Jun, first idiqut, takes the Turfan basin and Beshbalik. 'In 866, Pugu Jun declared himself khan and adopted the title of idiqut. The Kingdom of Qocho captured Xizhou (Gaochang), Tingzhou (Beshbalik, or Beiting), Changbaliq (near Ürümqi) and Luntai (Bugur) from the Guiyi Circuit.' The Guiyi page has Xizhou 'taken by the Uyghurs in 866'. Cliopatria's shape already holds this land from 860.
876: Qocho seizes Hami. 'In 876, the Kingdom of Qocho seized Yizhou from the Guiyi Circuit'; the Guiyi page: 'Yizhou fell to the Qocho Uyghurs in 876'. Cliopatria's shape leaves Hami out.
904: the Guiyi Circuit occupies Hami and Gaochang. 'In 904, Zhang Chengfeng of the Guiyi Circuit (later renamed Jinshan Kingdom) attacked Qocho and seized Yizhou (Hami/Kumul) and Xizhou (Gaochang).'
911: the occupation ends. 'This occupation ended after the Jinshan Kingdom's loss to the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom in 911.' The page does not give the year of the Uyghur return.

By 1096: Qocho loses Kucha and Aksu to the Kara-Khanids. 'By 1096, Qocho had lost Aksu, Tumshuk, and Kucha to the Kara-Khanid Khanate.' The page gives no year for the loss; the counterpart slug is the Eastern Kara-Khanids because Cliopatria's Eastern row (1046-1138) is the Kara-Khanid row that touches Qocho (the seed neighbours).

ledger.note: 1128: Qocho becomes a Qara Khitai vassal and goes on. 'In 1128, the Kingdom of Qocho became a vassal of the Qara Khitai' ('In 1128, during the reign of Bilge Tekin, the Uighur Kingdom became a vassal state of the Western Liao', which at first 'exercised only a loose control'); the infobox says 'Vassal state of the Western Liao (1132-1209)'. The Qara Khitai page (second page) dates the vassalization of 'the Kingdom of Qocho' to 1134 and has Yelu Dashi 'suzerain of Qocho' within a year of 1130, so the year is 1128-1134 on the pages; 1128 is the Qocho article's body text. Fixed after review: this was typed dissolve and the life ended in 1128.

wars.name: Qocho conquest of the Guiyi Circuit's Xizhou and Tingzhou

zones.text: Xizhou, Tingzhou, Changbaliq, Luntai and Yizhou

wars.outcome: Qocho took Gaochang, Beshbalik, Changbaliq and Luntai in 866 and Hami in 876; attacks on the Guiyi Circuit were repelled in 869-870 and Shazhou in 880.

wars.name: Guiyi occupation of Hami and Gaochang
wars.outcome: Zhang Chengfeng of the Guiyi Circuit seized Yizhou and Xizhou in 904; the occupation ended after the Ganzhou Uyghurs defeated the Jinshan Kingdom in 911.
wars.note: Ganzhou page: 'In 911 the Ganzhou Uyghurs attacked the Kingdom of Jinshan and forced them into an alliance as a lesser partner'.

wars.name: Kara-Khanid conquest of Kucha and Aksu
wars.outcome: By 1096 Qocho had lost Aksu, Tumshuk and Kucha to the Kara-Khanid Khanate.
wars.note: The fighting is undated: the page's sentence is 'By 1096' (it follows the 1068 accession of Tengri Uighur Tarkan and precedes the 1123 rise of Bilga).

certainty.note: Oasis cities of the Tarim's northern rim and the Turfan basin with the Tianshan steppe; Cliopatria holds one shape for 280 years and no page gives a frontier.
Vassal centuries (Qara Khitai, Mongols, Chagatai): the kingdom kept its idiqut, no page gives a frontier or an extent, and the shape is the 1126 one carried forward.

notes:
Pages opened: Qocho (three reads), Guiyi Circuit, and on the repair pass Qara Khitai, Chagatai Khanate and Tarim Basin (5 distinct pages, budget 5).
Start moved from Cliopatria's 860 to 843 (infobox) with a new keyframe for Karashahr and Kucha: the page puts Turfan, Beshbalik and Changbaliq in 866, so Cliopatria's 860 shape is 6 years early for them. The Guiyi page has Xizhou (Gaochang) captured by the Guiyi Circuit in 851 and 'taken by the Uyghurs in 866'.
End moved from Cliopatria's 1138 to 1370 (repair pass, review ia-01-f): 1128 was a vassalage, not an end. Qocho page: 1128 vassal of the Qara Khitai (infobox 1132; Qara Khitai page 1134), 1209 allegiance to Genghis Khan (infobox Mongol vassalage 1209-1335), 'Later ... part of the Chagatai Khanate' (undated; the Chagatai page does not mention Qocho), last known ruler 1352, 'By the 1370s ... ceased to exist', infobox 'Disestablished: 14th century'. The end year 1370 and the 1335 Chagatai start are confidence-1 bridges. Other dossiers should carry the matching events: kara-khitans (ia-01-g) vassal_start 1128 (or 1132/1134) and vassal_end 1209 naming qocho-kingdom; mongol-empire vassal_start 1209; chagatai-khanate vassal_start/dissolve. Cliopatria's Kara-Khitans shape contains the whole Qocho shape from 1139, so the map paints the vassal as direct Qara Khitai land unless the vassal tint is applied.
Cliopatria's shape includes 213 Gansu cells east of Hami that belong to the Guiyi Circuit (Shazhou, Guazhou side) and leaves Hami out; both are corrected. The loss of Kucha and Aksu by 1096 is on the page but not in Cliopatria.
Disagreement: the Qara Khitai vassalage year, 1128 in the body and 1132 in the infobox. No area on the page, so no infobox comparison. Dynasty list not recorded (idiqut names appear only from 1229). Counterparts without dossiers: guiyi-circuit (848-1036, Dunhuang), tibetan-empire exists (ea-04). Gazetteer: 'Tumshuk', 'Luntai', 'Changbaliq' are not places; Karashahr, Gaochang, Beshbalik, Hami, Kuqa, Aksu, Ürümqi are.
Repair pass (review ia-01-f): applied the three fixes (ledger/6 retyped vassal_start and the life extended to 1370 with the 1209, 1335 and 1370 events and a new 1139-1369 keyframe; keyframe 1040-1125 no longer removes Kucha and Aksu before the 1096 loss; keyframe 860 states that it applies from 866). The wars/2 slug fix was already applied by the reviewer. Not settled: who held Aksu and Kucha before 1096 (Tarim Basin page silent; Cliopatria's Khotan row has Aksu to 1009 while the Qocho page has Qocho losing it 'by 1096', so the dossier keeps Aksu in Qocho's shape from 888 as Cliopatria draws it and the kingdom-of-khotan dossier is not changed); the extent of the kingdom in 1139-1369; the Yuan period is typed under mongol-empire for 1209-1335 following the infobox, and a gap-filler may split it at 1294 (yuan-dynasty) if the colour agent needs it.
